page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16 GB of system memory. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The hardware configuration includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU metrics, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the top tier. However, multi-core scaling shows some limitations; stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores fall into the average tier, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression drops to the bottom 25%. Memory performance is mixed, with small-block cached read bandwidth performing at an average level of 418.9 GB/sec, whereas large-block uncached read bandwidth is weak at 37.73 GB/sec.

The instance is suited for workloads such as static web serving, Redis database operations, and lightweight single-threaded processing tasks, where it achieves average to top-tier throughput. It is less suited for memory-intensive large-block operations or complex multi-threaded tasks due to the noted memory bandwidth and multi-core scaling bottlenecks. For machine learning, it handles small-model LLM inference at average speeds but exhibits poor performance during prompt processing on medium-sized models.
